title: Derived dg-module tensor and its flat bar model
statement:
Use the cochain convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and small dg categories over $\mathbf Z$ as in [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure]. Let $\mathcal B$ be such a category, $G$ a right dg $\mathcal B$-module and $F$ a left dg $\mathcal B$-module: their values are cochain complexes, with unital associative chain-map actions $G(V)\otimes\mathcal B(U,V)\to G(U)$ and $\mathcal B(U,V)\otimes F(U)\to F(V)$. Their balanced tensor is the direct sum $\bigoplus_U G(U)\otimes F(U)$ modulo $(ga)\otimes f=g\otimes(af)$. A semi-free module has an exhaustive increasing filtration starting at zero, split on underlying graded modules, whose successive dg quotients are direct sums of shifted representables; such replacements exist by [lem-coef-dg-module-semi-free-replacement], also for left modules by passage to the opposite category. Tensoring either semi-free input with an objectwise quasi-isomorphism of the other input is a quasi-isomorphism. If $P\to G$ and $Q\to F$ are semi-free replacements, then
$$P\otimes_{\mathcal B}F\ \longleftarrow\ P\otimes_{\mathcal B}Q\ \longrightarrow\ G\otimes_{\mathcal B}Q$$
are quasi-isomorphisms. They define the derived balanced tensor, natural in the two modules and invariant under objectwise quasi-isomorphisms in both inputs.

Assume in addition that every $\mathcal B(U,V)$ is homotopically flat over $\mathbf Z$, meaning its tensor with any acyclic complex is acyclic, and that at least one of $F,G$ is objectwise homotopically flat over $\mathbf Z$. The unnormalized two-sided bar total complex $B(G,\mathcal B,F)$ represents $G\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal B}F$. Its simplicial degree $n\geq0$ is
$$\bigoplus_{U_0,\ldots,U_n}G(U_n)\otimes\mathcal B(U_{n-1},U_n)\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal B(U_0,U_1)\otimes F(U_0),$$
Write this tensor complex as $V_n$ and put $B=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}V_n[n]$, so simplicial degree $n$ lowers the cochain degree by $n$. On $V_n[n]$ the internal differential is $(-1)^n d_{V_n}$. For $n\geq1$ its other component is $\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^i\partial_i:V_n[n]\to V_{n-1}[n-1]$: numbering the factors from the left by $0,\ldots,n+1$, $\partial_i$ merges adjacent factors $i,i+1$ by the right action when $i=0$, composition when $0<i<n$, and the left action when $i=n$. This component is zero on $V_0$. Degeneracies insert units. The augmentation to $G\otimes_{\mathcal B}F$ is the quotient map on $V_0$ and zero on $V_n$ for $n>0$. The comparison with the derived balanced tensor is natural in module maps. The complex $B[1]$, rather than $B$, has $n+1$ suspensions in the summand indexed by $V_n$.

source.place: Drinfeld §§14.3-14.8 (balanced tensor, semi-free homotopical flatness), §3.6(i) (bar model under flatness), and §1.3.1. Supports prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint proof paragraph 2: derived evaluation of the restricted representable modules.
